After the Owner deposits 1 wei and calls Command with 0 wei, the reference's withdraw() sends 1 wei to Owner (balance becomes 1), while the bug's withdraw() sends 0 (balance stays 0).

After depositing 1 ether via receive() and calling Command(address(this), '') with msg.value = 0, the reference contract (>=) transfers the whole balance (0) when msg.value equals the contract balance (both 1 ether), leaving address(c).balance = 0, while the buggy contract (>) does not execute the transfer because the condition is false, leaving address(c).balance = 1 ether.

After depositing 1 ether via receive() and calling Command(address(this),'') with msg.value = 1 ether (so msg.value == address(this).balance), the reference contract transfers all balance via multiplicate, leaving balance 0, while the buggy contract does not transfer, leaving balance 1 ether.

After sending 2 ether to the contract via receive() and then calling Command(address(this),'') with msg.value = 1 ether and only 1 ether in the contract balance, the reference contract (>=) triggers multiplicate when msg.value equals contract balance, leaving address(c).balance = 0; the buggy contract (>) does not trigger, leaving address(c).balance = 1 ether.

After funding the contract with 2 ether via receive(), then calling Command(address(this),"") with msg.value = 2 ether (so msg.value equals contract balance), the reference contract (>=) triggers multiplicate and transfers the entire 4 ether to address(this), leaving address(this).balance = 0, while the buggy version (>) does not trigger the transfer, leaving address(this).balance = 2 ether.

After depositing 2 ether into the contract via Command and then calling multiplicate with 1 ether, the reference contract sends the full balance (3 ether) to the destination address, while the buggy contract sends only 1 ether, leaving 2 ether in the contract.

After deploying C, sending 2 ether via Command, then calling multiplicate with 2 ether to an external address, the reference contract transfers all 4 ether (leaving 0 balance) while the buggy contract transfers only 2 ether (leaving 2 ether in the contract).

After sending 2 ether via Command and then calling multiplicate with 2 ether, the reference contract transfers the full 4 ether to the destination (leaving 0 balance), while the buggy contract transfers only 2 ether (leaving 2 ether in the contract).

After sending 1 ether via Command and then calling multiplicate with 1 ether, the reference contract transfers the full 2 ether to the destination (leaving 0 balance), while the buggy contract transfers only 1 ether (leaving 1 ether in the contract).

After sending 2 ether via Command and then calling multiplicate with 2 ether, the reference contract transfers the full 4 ether to the destination (leaving 0 balance), while the buggy contract transfers only 2 ether (leaving 2 ether in the contract).
